# RPC overnight pass — ledger

Rolling record of items the nightly autonomous pass has shipped / queued / declined. The night pass reads this fully before acting and never re-suggests anything under "Declined — do not re-suggest" (that heading is Trevor's to edit).

Format per item: date · status · what · revert path (if shipped) · target metric · night-count (if queued).

> 🚨 **`git revert <sha>` paths in entries dated BEFORE 2026-08-03 are DEAD — the shas no longer resolve.** The `git filter-repo` + force-push on 2026-08-03 (purging leaked live Dapper session cookies, `ba6ffef2`) rewrote every pre-purge commit sha. Measured 2026-08-03: 11 of 12 spot-checked shas across this file + CLAUDE.md are gone. **Do not conclude a commit never existed** — find it by its commit MESSAGE (`git log --grep=...`), or recover the old→new mapping from the Vercel deployment list, which still stores each old sha next to its full commit message. **The DB half of every revert path is unaffected** (revert SQL names functions/tables, not shas).

🚨 **EVERY TIME YOU REPORT TO TREVOR IS PT — chat and summaries too, not just these headings. NEVER quote a UTC/`Z` time to him.** **Dates are Pacific (Trevor's timezone). The sandbox/CI clock is UTC (~7–8h ahead), so convert to PT before stamping a dated `###` heading.** A UTC clock on the 29th before ~07:00Z is still the 28th in PT. ⚠ **On Trevor's Windows box the ONLY trustworthy clock is PowerShell `Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm zzz"` — it prints the offset, so it cannot be wrong silently.** Both Git Bash forms lie: `TZ=America/Los_Angeles date` returns UTC labelled `GMT` (no `/usr/share/zoneinfo`), and plain `date` returns UTC with **NO zone label at all** — measured in the same minute 2026-08-10, a full calendar day apart. In a UTC sandbox, subtract 7h (PDT) / 8h (PST) from `date -u` by hand.

### 2026-11-07 · 🔧 SHIPPED (code) — **Third fresh-eyes review: the trade room + Trade Block (the no-custody swap surface, signing live since 10-31). Ten findings, all ten fixed, each pinned by a test proven red on the old code** (Claude Code cloud, ~11:10 AM–12:30 PM PT). **The proposal contract (`lib/trade-room/store.ts`):** (1) `touch()` wrote the room `status` from the caller's SNAPSHOT under a version-only check, and join / cancel never bump the version — an edit loaded before B joined wrote "open" back (accept's lock could then never match: a stuck room), and an edit loaded before a cancel revived it as "building". Edits now `claimEdit` (version CAS + `status IN editable`, no status write) → write → `finishEdit` (bump again, clear acceptances again); the only status an edit writes is accepted → building, conditional on itself. (2) `setItems`/`setWallet` wrote rows BEFORE the version CAS, so a stale edit's rows landed under the winner's version (B could accept v6 showing X while the room held Y) — the claim now comes first and a loser writes nothing; the second bump voids any Accept that read the room mid-write. (3) two Accepts in the same second each saw the other as null and neither locked — `accept()` re-reads the sides after its own write. (4) ⛔ **a cancel after the co-signer SIGNED** recorded a trade that then sealed on chain as "cancelled" and emailed "Nothing moved": cancel is refused (409 `cosigned`) while `signing` with a signature inside the relay window (15 min; a failed read refuses too), and `sealed` / `markSealed` now record a chain-proven seal even over a `cancelled` row (the chain outranks the cancel). (5) the `items` action capped picks only AFTER the wmc reads and per-collection chain scripts — capped before any read now. **Trade Block:** (6) `decide()` created the room BEFORE claiming the proposal, so a double-click opened two live rooms (an orphan in both users' lists, counting toward the live-room cap) — the proposal is claimed first; a room-setup failure hands the proposal back to pending and cancels the half-made room. ### 2026-11-06 · 🔒 SHIPPED (dependency, key path) — **Hot-wallet signer moves off `elliptic` (CVE-2025-14505 / GHSA-848j-6mx2-7j84, no patched release) to `@noble/curves` 1.9.7 — output BYTE-IDENTICAL; uuid 11.1.0 → 11.1.1 and @babel/core → 7.29.7 lockfile bumps** (Claude Code cloud, ~1:25 PM PT; Trevor: "work on this and anything else relevant"). **Measured before deciding:** the advisory's nonce truncation fires only when the curve order's bit length is not a multiple of 8 — elliptic vs noble RFC 6979 on secp256k1: 0 of 20,000 signatures diverged; positive control P-521: 11 of 3,000 (~1/256, the bug's rate). So the hot wallet (`0x3aa11c84d776838f`, secp256k1) was never exposed; the swap removes an unpatched, unmaintained library from the key path. `lib/breaks/server-authz.ts signWithKey` → `secp256k1.sign(digest, pk, { lowS: false })` — `lowS:false` because elliptic never canonicalised S and that is the form verified on mainnet. `elliptic` + `@types/elliptic` removed (with bn.js / brorand / hash.js / hmac-drbg / minimalistic-*). Tests now verify with OpenSSL (`node:crypto`, independent of the signer, hashes the message itself) and pin 4 known-answer vectors produced by the elliptic signer before the swap (one high-S); planted defects caught: `lowS:true` → 1 red, SHA3-256 → 7 red. The other 3 alerts, re-derived: `deepmerge` is declared by `@onflow/sdk` but imported by NO `@onflow/*` bundle (unreachable; no fix exists); `uuid` 9.0.1 under `@onflow/sdk` is called only as `v4()` without a buffer (advisory covers v3/v5/v6 with a caller buffer; fix is a major); `minimatch` is eslint dev-only (fix is a major). ### 2026-11-03 · 🔧 SHIPPED (laptop runner) + 📏 ROOT CAUSE — **Panini's "slow TOP" was the runner's long-lived Chrome tab: every run now opens a fresh tab, and the serial-paging script is bounded** (Claude Code local, ~4:05–4:35 PM PT; Trevor: "keep going … work on what you can"). The 4:00 PM run on `c02ce193e` captured no RECENT in its first 11 cards. Probes in separate tabs of the same panini-cdp-profile Chrome showed Panini answering TOP in 0.1–0.2 s and RECENT in 0.1 s, even after serial paging. A replay of the runner's exact per-card sequence also captured both in < 1 s. **A/B, one card, the same code, alternated twice:** on the tab the runner reuses run after run (`ctx.pages().find(...)`), serial paging took **27 s** and the sales tab never fired in time (no TOP, no RECENT); on a fresh tab, **3.5 s**, and both lists landed in 0.7 s. `bfe6467`, `9dcf8ae` and `c02ce193e` had all read that tab's slowness as Panini's. Fix (`scripts/ingest-panini-runner.mjs`): over CDP the run opens its own tab (`openRunnerPage`), records its CDP target id in `~/.panini-runner-tab.json`, and closes it on every exit path (end, stall, both early exits). A tab left by a crashed run is closed at the next start BY TARGET ID, never by evaluating in other tabs; page recovery opens a fresh tab too. `loadAllSerialPages`' in-page loop, the walk's last untimed call, now races a cap of max × (wait + 200 ms) + 10 s. ### 2026-11-03 · 🔧 SHIPPED (laptop runner) + 📏 CORRECTION of `9dcf8ae` — **The "stale previous-card" sales read is the previous card's OWN slow TOP request, not an SPA stale read; the runner now reads RECENT as soon as the tab fires and gives TOP a bounded grace (no re-click)** (Claude Code local, on the laptop, ~3:25–3:35 PM PT; Trevor: "keep going"). The 2:00 PM run, the first on `9dcf8ae`, was worse: progress 50 at 23 min and 100 at 42 min (19 min per 50 cards; 8–12 pre-11-03, 17 at noon), with 121 sale records per 100 cards (1.2/card; ~6.4 at 8:00 AM). It is the request the walk left behind; its body read fails on navigation and `captureOp` stamps it with the new URL. 85 cards had only that; 15 got their own TOP (3.7–11.6 s after load) and then RECENT ~0.7 s later. So TOP is slow or never answers, RECENT is fast, and `9dcf8ae`'s two re-clicks (4 s each) fired more slow TOPs and then skipped RECENT, the list that moves coverage. Other-card answers are now `late_responses`; the log adds `top_answered=` / `top_unanswered=`; the ops capture adds `ms` (request start → body) per op. The test `panini-runner-sales-wait-counts-only-this-cards-answer` was inverted (re-click → no re-click, RECENT before the TOP grace); a planted grace-before-RECENT reds it. **Judge:** the 4:00 PM run. Now an insert-only upsert on the unique key `(owner_key, channel, alert_kind, subject_key, dedup_bucket)` with `status='sending'` precedes the send; no row back = another run holds it (counted `already_sent_this_week`); a claim error refuses the send (fails closed); a failed send DELETEs the claim; success updates it to `sent`. `claim_pending_deliveries` claims only `pending`, so the drain never picks a `sending` digest row. ### 2026-10-30 · 🔧 SHIPPED (code) — **Low-priority seeded wallets refresh every 24 h again, not 36 h; this was behind the Cadence Collapse critical** (Claude Code cloud, 8:01 AM PT). Sentinel paged CRITICAL: seven `wallet-backfill*` lanes at 40 % of baseline, "a caller fault". The caller is healthy (every `seed-wallet-refresh` wave `ok`, 0 errors). The cause is the low-priority gate in `/api/seed-wallet-refresh`: it skips a wallet walked under 24 h ago, and waves run 12 h apart (since 07-18). A walk stamps a few minutes after its wave, so 24 h later the wallet reads 23 h 5x min, gets skipped, and waits for the next wave: a 36 h cycle, against the "~24h" the code documents. Measured: all 191 active low-priority wallets were walked 10-29 5:46–6:31 AM PT and skipped by the 10-30 5:45–6:27 AM PT waves (low_priority_skipped ~48 per cohort, against 0 on 10-29). The gate now counts a wallet due within 2 h of the interval (`LOW_PRIORITY_DUE_TOLERANCE_MS`). Waves fire on exact cron-job.org minutes, so 2 h can never let a wallet run twice in one 12 h period. Cost: restores the documented daily cadence for ~191 wallets (it had been running at 2/3 of that by accident). Test: `api-seed-wallet-refresh-deep` +1 (a wallet walked 23 h 59 m ago is due, one walked 20 h ago is not); reverting the tolerance (a planted defect) reds it. **Watch:** the 5:45 PM PT wave walks these wallets anyway (36 h). The proof is the 10-31 5:45 AM PT wave: low_priority_skipped ≈ 0, with ~258 walks across its cohorts. **Revert:** `git revert`, or set `SEED_REFRESH_LOWPRI_INTERVAL_HOURS=26` in Vercel.

### 2026-10-29 · 🔧 SHIPPED (DB) — **The on-chain subedition resolver works first-in-first-out; it had been starving the newest Moments** (Cowork cloud, ~2:36–3:00 PM PT; the scheduled check-in on the 10-28 Animated / Illustrated work).
- **The check found the 1:32 PM resolver run had resolved its full 20,000 but none of the 155 Animated / Illustrated moments queued at 9:55 PM 10-28.**
  - Cause: `get_topshot_subedition_targets()` picks `ORDER BY nft_id`, and `nft_id` is TEXT. So the order is lexicographic, and each day's "1…"–"3…" inflow fills the batch first.
  - Measured after the run: all 10,000 still-pending rows had ids starting 4–8 (4,682 × "4…", 5,281 × "5…"). That is the NEWEST Moments, current series and new parallels included.
  - The 20260904133105 queue-cap design had reasoned about numeric order.
- **Fix (`20261029213925`):**
  - `topshot_moment_subeditions.queued_at` (DEFAULT now(); a STABLE default is catalog-only, no rewrite).
  - A partial index on `(queued_at, nft_id) WHERE subedition_id IS NULL`.
  - The batch ordered by `(queued_at, nft_id)`. Inflow is ~25k/day against 20k resolved, so every id now waits ~1–2 days at worst.

### 2026-10-29 · 🔧 SHIPPED (DB) — **An FMV's basis age is never younger than its last sale** (Cowork cloud, ~8:45–9:00 AM PT; follow-up to the entry below). ### 2026-10-28 · 🔧 SHIPPED (code + DB) — **FMV snapshots stop publishing a false "last sale" age and a zeroed 30-day count: two ages, two columns** (Cowork cloud, ~10:35–11:00 PM PT; Trevor: "Dig deeper"). Found while checking the new Animated editions' prices; it affects the whole estate.
- **The engine defect:** `fmv-recalc`'s main loop stamped `days_since_sale` from the grail-spike-CLEANED pricing set. When an edition's only recent sale was a stripped spike, the column read the age of an older sale. Examples: a #3 at $8.90 over a $1 cluster, a #1/5 at $150, a #99/99 last mint.
- **Who reads it as the last sale's age:**
  - the edition page prints "last sale N days ago";
  - the moment page hides the 30-day count by it;
  - `fmv_snapshots_zero_stale_sales_count` zeroes `sales_count_30d` whenever it exceeds 30.
- **Measured** over the latest snapshot per edition (3 days): 103 Top Shot + 30 All Day editions overstated their last-sale age by more than 2 days, and 28 published "no sale in 30 days" over a real one. None were HIGH or MEDIUM. Example: `250:8569::18` sold #3 for $8.90 on 10-22, then read LOW at $0.75, "52 days" and 0 sales for a week.
- **The fix — two ages, two columns:**
  - `days_since_sale` is now the age of the true last market sale (market sales after the mis-key guard, before cleaning).
  - The new `fmv_snapshots.basis_days_since_sale` holds the age of the newest sale the PRICE rests on.
  - The sniper's staleness penalty is about the price's evidence, so it reads the basis age, through a new `get_editions_latest_fmv_wide_v2` (v1 is unchanged for `/api/fmv`, wallet-search and cache-refresh), and falls back to `days_since_sale`. The sniper is exactly as conservative as before, and the deal still displays the true age.
  - Writers that don't separate the two leave the basis NULL.
- **The historical-fallback step had the same false zero.** It hardcoded `sales_count_7d/30d = 0` even when the last sale was 7–29 days old: 2–9 editions a day, including our 5 Animated editions (e.g. `274:9079::23`, sold 10-13, published 10-28 as "0 sales in 30 days"). It now writes 0 only once the sale's age proves it (≥ 7 days for the 7-day count, ≥ 30 for the 30-day count), and NULL otherwise. The stale guard leaves a NULL count's label alone.
- **Migration** `20261029054916`: ADD COLUMN plus the v2 function. A DROP + CREATE of v1 was "cancelled" twice by the MCP's destructive-statement gate, so v2 is a new name. EXECUTE is service_role only (anon false, verified).
- **Tests:**
  - the 1.8.3 spike fixture now asserts days 2 / basis 35 / count 1, with a control where the two ages agree;
  - the historical step has 3 age cases;
  - the sniper has a pass-through spy on `applyFmvStalenessPenalty` (basis 40 → 40; NULL or absent → 2) and asserts the displayed age;
  - each was red with its old line planted back.

**Revert:** `git revert` the commit, then `DROP FUNCTION public.get_editions_latest_fmv_wide_v2(uuid[]); ALTER TABLE public.fmv_snapshots DROP COLUMN basis_days_since_sale;` (through the SQL editor; the MCP refuses DROP).

### 2026-10-27 · 🧭 SHIPPED (code only) — **A failed wallet walk no longer records a "scan" (write-side honesty: `wallet_backfill_state` stamped verified-with-0 after failures)** (Claude Code cloud, ~7:35–8:00 AM PT).
- **Defect:** all five wallet-backfill routes (Top Shot, All Day, Golazos, Pinnacle ×2 modes, UFC) called `record_wallet_backfill_scan` after EVERY run, whatever happened. A failed walk therefore set `last_scanned_at = now()`, `last_found_count = 0`. Readers take that row as a measurement: `check_wmc_ownership_freshness` ("fully re-enumerated"), `reconcile_allow_list_prewarm` (0 ⇒ "reconciled_empty", marks prewarm complete), `golazos-discover-buyers` (a row ⇒ never re-selected). **Measured:** the 29 UFC walks that failed on Flow 429s 10-26 (4:36–5:17 PM PT) — **29 of 29 stamped `found 0` after the failure, none walked successfully since** (all 29 hold 0 UFC rows, so today's damage is a false freshness/prewarm claim, not lost holdings). The 429 cause itself was already fixed by `0212d78a8` (10-26 5:38 PM PT, retry); this closes the shape for every other failure.
- **Fix:** `BackfillRunResult.scanned` (+ `runIdOnlyBackfill` and the Top Shot walker): true only when holdings were fully read AND written (or the wallet provably lacks the collection, or the ID read proved it empty); false on lock skip, storage/computation limit, unenumerable getIDs, flow timeout, hard error, chunk write errors, or an unfinished checkpoint pass. Routes record only when `scanned`. 30 return sites set explicitly.
- **Tests:** helper expectations carry `scanned`; route tests invert "lock skip records 0" and assert no record on storage-limit / hard error / unfinished checkpoint, with no-capability as the control that still records; new tree-walk guard `wallet-scan-record-gated-on-scanned` (derived population — it found the All Day route I had missed; planted ungated UFC call reds it). Preflight 6/6 green.
- **Behaviour change to watch:** a wallet that fails every walk (e.g. the one All Day/Golazos `unenumerable_getids_over_script_limit` wallet, 2 Top Shot `computation_limit_exceeded` wallets) now ages in `wallet_backfill_state` instead of reading fresh. Nothing alarms on that function; `seed-wallet-refresh` uses the newest stamp across collections. Falsifier = a selector re-dispatching the same failing wallet every tick (`pipeline_runs` repeats per wallet climbing).
- **Revert:** `git revert` the "fix(wallet-backfill): record a scan only when the walk scanned" commit.

### 2026-10-25 · 🔒 SHIPPED (code) — **Same-origin XSS through the IPFS media proxy closed: `/api/public/ipfs-media/<cid>` streamed ANY content type from a caller-chosen CID under our origin; it now serves only raster images and video, and every media-proxy path gets a script-less `sandbox` CSP** (Claude Code cloud, ~2:47–2:55 PM PT; Trevor: "Keep going"). Found while sweeping SSRF / redirect surfaces (the auth redirects and `avatar-media` were already hardened). The route passed the gateway's `content-type` straight through, so anyone could pin an HTML file (or an SVG with `<script>`) to IPFS and send someone `https://www.rippackscity.com/api/public/ipfs-media/<cid>`: the page would render as rippackscity.com under the site CSP (`script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`), with the visitor's session cookies and, for you, the admin session in localStorage. No sign of use: 7 days of `[ipfs-media] ok` lines show only `image/png` / `image/jpeg`. Two layers now: (1) `lib/media/servable-media-type.ts` — png/jpeg/gif/webp/avif/mp4/webm/quicktime are streamed, anything else 302s to the gateway (runs, if at all, on the gateway's origin); (2) `proxy.ts` sends `MEDIA_PROXY_CSP` (`default-src 'none'; … sandbox`, no script source) on every `MEDIA_PROXY_PREFIXES` path (ipfs-media, ipfs-thumb, avatar-media, pinnacle-image, team-logo, badge-image — whose Dapper SVGs were the same shape with a trusted upstream —, moment-thumbnail, og). Subresource loads are unaffected (a response's CSP does not govern how a page embeds it). Tests: 3 route cases (html / svg / octet-stream → 302 to the gateway, body cancelled) red on the old route; a proxy-dispatch case reds on the old proxy; type-allowlist unit cases. Revert: `git revert` the code commit.

### 2026-07-16 (Claude Code, interactive, afternoon) — night-queue Item 1 SHIPPED: `get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite kills the #1 disk reader (1,522 MB/193s → 8.4 MB/119ms)

Worked the 07-16 night handoff ([docs/handoff-2026-07-16-evening-queue.md](../archive/handoffs/handoff-2026-07-16-evening-queue.md)) top item — the post-wmc-fix #1 pg_stat_statements reader. Shipped **1** (DB-only, 1 index + 1 fn rewrite), reverted 0. Pure DB; no code deploy. Ledger is the record.

- **SHIPPED — `get_lock_check_batch` index-driven rewrite** (migrations `audit_20260716_wmc_lockcheck_order_index` + `audit_20260716_get_lock_check_batch_index_driven_rewrite`). The old body window-ranked the ENTIRE stale `wallet_moments_cache` set (~2.0M rows) per call with a per-row `EXISTS(hot_wallets)` subplan in both the SELECT and the window `ORDER BY`, then `LIMIT p_limit` — measured **1,522 MB read / 193s in a single call** (historic 1,286 GB / 1,460 calls). It was the driver of the hourly IOPS-saturation windows (page-view 30s statement-timeouts + smoke pages). New body: index `idx_wmc_lockcheck_order (collection_id, lock_checked_at ASC NULLS FIRST)` (14 MB) + two index-driven arms per collection off that index — (a) fill = the p_limit stalest rows in the collection, (b) priority = the p_limit stalest rows owned by a hot wallet (472 hot addrs, materialized once) — `UNION ALL`, dedup (`bool_or` reconstructs `is_priority` with **no** per-row EXISTS), then rank priority-first/stalest-first per collection and round-robin via `ORDER BY rn, collection_id`. **Identical batch semantics** to the old body (validated pre-swap: golazos scoped old-vs-new = 44/44 rows, 0 set diff, 0 priority-flag mismatch; + composition proof — each arm capped at p_limit is sufficient because the final batch is ≤ p_limit total). **EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS)** unscoped/limit200: `Index Scan using idx_wmc_lockcheck_order` on both arms, **shared hit=690 read=383 (~8.4 MB) / Execution 119 ms** (was 1,522 MB / 193,000 ms → ~180× fewer reads, ~1,600× faster). Live fn verified: 200 rows / 5 collections / 0 null keys / priority-first (matches old ranking); SECDEF + ACL `postgres`+`service_role` only (no anon/authenticated). Route unchanged (still reads the same 4 out_ cols).
  - **Build note (reusable):** MCP `execute_sql` wraps multi-statement calls in a txn (→ `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` 25001); a lone-statement CONCURRENTLY avoids the txn but is still 2min-capped and one full 785 MB wmc scan already exceeds 2 min under contention → canceled → invalid 0-byte index. Built instead via `apply_migration` plain `CREATE INDEX` in a verified-idle window (active=0) guarded by `SET LOCAL lock_timeout='4s'` + `maintenance_work_mem='128MB'`; completed <2 min, `indisvalid=true`. See [[route-db-calls-inherit-8s-statement-timeout]].
  - **Revert:** `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.idx_wmc_lockcheck_order;` + recreate the prior `get_lock_check_batch` body from migration history (the `WITH hot_wallets … ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY collection_id ORDER BY EXISTS(...) DESC, lock_checked_at NULLS FIRST)` window version).
  - **Target metric:** `get_lock_check_batch` drops out of the top of `pg_stat_statements` by shared_blks_read/call (≈0.9 GB/call → <0.02 GB/call); the hourly page-view statement-timeout bursts + smoke saturation windows stop; `lock-check-batch` pipeline stays ok=true.

### 2026-07-12 (Claude Code, interactive) — Cross-session `main` auto-sync: SessionStart hook shipped to `main` (`e01575ab`)

Trevor: "get local main to stop falling behind and continuously stay synced across all mains." **Diagnosis:** the alarming "50 ahead / 50 behind" on local `main` was a **shallow-clone illusion** — web sessions clone this repo shallow (~50 deep) and start on a fresh `claude/*` branch, so the true merge-base sits below the fetch horizon and git falsely reports divergence. After `git fetch --unshallow`, local `main` was **0 ahead / 110 behind** = pure ancestor, just stale, no lost work, no conflicts. One-time fix applied live (`git branch -f main origin/main`).

- **SHIPPED (infra) — `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` + `.claude/settings.json` (`e01575ab`).** SessionStart hook (web-only, synchronous, idempotent) runs every session: unshallows the clone so relationships compute truthfully → fast-forwards local `main` to `origin/main` with `--ff-only` (**never** clobbers genuine unpushed commits — leaves them with a notice) → checks out `main` on a clean tree (per CLAUDE.md "always work on main"). `.gitignore` narrowed from `.claude/` to un-ignore ONLY those two shared files; local `.claude/` state stays ignored. Validated: caught a live `origin/main` advance (`d2b0eab2`→`a7421ee7`) and ff'd automatically; claude/*→main checkout path + non-remote guard both pass. **NOTE for nightly pass / monitor:** `.claude/hooks/` + `.claude/settings.json` are now TRACKED files — expected, not drift. **Revert:** `git rm -r .claude/hooks .claude/settings.json` + restore `.gitignore` line 52 to `.claude/`, or `git revert e01575ab`.

Full write-up: [docs/research/topshot-bulk-purchasing-reverse-engineering-2026-07-12.md](../research/topshot-bulk-purchasing-reverse-engineering-2026-07-12.md).

Picked up `docs/handoff-2026-07-12-*` (the overnight cron-failure investigation). Shipped the one blocked code item, then verified the DB-side fixes — and found the primary one never worked.

- **SHIPPED (code) — buyer-backfill forward lane bound to 2025+ (`44d741e`, prod `dpl_CEZHf4k6...` READY).** Added `.gte("sold_at", '2025-01-01')` to the forward null-buyer select in `app/api/admin/backfill-topshot-buyers/route.ts` (uses existing `HIST_WINDOW_END`) + `app/api/admin/backfill-allday-buyers/route.ts` (new `FORWARD_WINDOW_START` const). Stops the forward lane churning ~1.03M unreachable pre-current-spork null-buyer rows (rows_written≈0); planner now partition-prunes to `sales_2025/2026`. `tsc --noEmit` clean. Pairs with the 7 per-partition null-buyer indexes shipped DB-side. **Revert:** `git revert 44d741e`.
- **FINDING — the 2026-07-12 pg_cron `statement_timeout` fix (`audit_20260712_pgcron_stmt_timeout_and_stagger`) was INERT.** Heavy jobs were STILL dying at exactly 120s as recently as 14:03Z today (`cross-source-dedup`, `fmv-clamp`, `thin-fmv-guard`, `remap-misattrib`, `ccm-step1`, etc.) — **plus 4 the handoff never listed** (`backfill-historical-pack-ev` 43, `allday-rollup-rip-value` 23, `refresh-mv-pack-ev-latest` 35, `allday-badge-low-ask-refresh` 31). Root cause: pg_cron sends its command as one **simple-query batch**, so `statement_timeout` is armed once at batch start from the SESSION default (120s cluster default). The inline `SET statement_timeout='600s'; SELECT fn()` prefix (and the 06-30 proconfig) never re-arms the already-running batch. Yesterday's "live validation" passed only because it ran through a normal client session (separate `SET` message), which is NOT how pg_cron executes.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — dedicated `cron_heavy` role (`audit_20260712_cron_heavy_role_statement_timeout`) + 15 jobs reassigned onto it.** The only lever that works is a role SESSION default applied at connect time. Created `CREATE ROLE cron_heavy LOGIN INHERIT` with `ALTER ROLE cron_heavy SET statement_timeout='600s'`, `GRANT cron_heavy TO postgres`, `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public/cron`, `EXECUTE` on the 15 SECDEF fns, `MAINTAIN` on `mv_allday_pack_ev_corrected` (job 28's direct `REFRESH…CONCURRENTLY`, which can't be fn-wrapped). Scoped so interactive `postgres` (MCP/migrations/dashboard) keeps the 120s admin ceiling. Reassigned all 15 heavy jobs to run as `cron_heavy` (bare commands; role default supplies 600s; the 07-12 staggered schedules preserved) → new jobids 60–74. pg_cron requires **superuser to change a job's username** (blocked), so the reassignment was done via unschedule-as-postgres + `SET ROLE cron_heavy` re-schedule.
- **VALIDATED on the real pg_cron path** (the step yesterday skipped): a probe job `SELECT pg_sleep(125)` running as `cron_heavy` **succeeded at 125.1s** — past the old 120s ceiling. (Also learned pg_cron here does NOT stack overlapping runs of the same job, so the 600s ceiling on the 10-min-cadence jobs 71/73 can't pile up.)
- **Note:** LOGIN was required — with NOLOGIN the pg_cron worker fails `connection failed`. cron_heavy has no password; Supabase's network layer gates actual connections.
- **Revert (restore prior postgres-owned jobs, i.e. the 120s-failing state):** `SET ROLE cron_heavy;` unschedule each of the 15 names; `RESET ROLE;` reschedule each as postgres with its command; then `DROP OWNED BY cron_heavy; REVOKE cron_heavy FROM postgres; DROP ROLE cron_heavy;`. (Migration + this entry hold the full job list.)
- **VERIFIED LIVE (15:40–15:44Z first ticks under `cron_heavy`, all previously dying at exactly 120s):** `backfill-historical-pack-ev` **succeeded 121.0s**, `refresh-mv-pack-ev-latest` **succeeded 379.1s** (then dropped to **2.8s** on its very next 15:53 tick — backlog drained), `cross-source-dedup` **succeeded 583.7s**, `allday-rollup-rip-value` **succeeded 387.7s**. Zero failures among cron_heavy jobs since the fix. End-to-end confirmed on real production jobs, not just the probe.
- **SHIPPED (DB) — swept 3 MORE jobs onto `cron_heavy` (`audit_20260712_cron_heavy_grant_three_more_jobs` + reschedule; now 18 total).** A post-fix audit for ANY postgres-owned job that hit the 120s wall in the last 24h caught three the handoff/first-pass missed — two that died specifically in the OVERNIGHT window: `rpc-recover-null-serial-sales` (job 38, `backfill_null_serial_sales_from_moments`, died 06:35Z), `rpc-roll-pack-ask-hourly-low` (job 9, `roll_pack_ask_hourly_low`, died 06:07Z), and `rpc-sync-allday-pack-dist-totals` (job 45, `sync_allday_pack_dist_totals`, died 15:42Z). All SECDEF/postgres-owned; granted EXECUTE + reassigned to cron_heavy with unchanged schedules/bare commands. **Buyer-backfill confirmed healthy post-deploy:** `topshot-buyer-backfill` ok=true 28.3s at 15:34Z (was ~97% failing pre-index).
- **RESOLVED — `cross-source-dedup` (job 67) backlog-drain confirmed one-time.** First post-fix run was 583.7s (had completed NOTHING while capped at 120s); the very next hourly tick (16:40Z) **succeeded in 40s** — steady-state is well under the 600s ceiling, so the timeout fix alone was sufficient and no dedup/`sales`-DELETE optimization is needed. **`check_pgcron_recent_failures()` has drained to 0** and `detect_stalled_pipelines()` = [] — the 120s-death class is eliminated across all 18 reassigned jobs.

### 2026-07-11 ~10:25 PT (Claude Code, interactive) — 3 failing pipelines fixed: pack-opens backfill lock-timeout (DB fix LIVE) + hydrator whole-chunk-discard (committed, needs deploy)

Trevor flagged 3 pipelines with 3 consecutive failures each. Diagnosed from live `pipeline_runs` (ground truth differed from the report: topshot backfill already `done`, allday failing with **lock** timeout not statement timeout). Commit `c1ba51e` (local `main`, **NOT pushed**). DB migration `audit_20260711_upsert_pack_rips_lock_timeout` **applied to remote (live now)**.

- **`pack-opens-api-backfill-{topshot,allday}` — "canceling statement due to lock timeout" ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (DB fix live).** Not a missing index (`idx_pack_rips_tx_hash` unique exists) and not statement timeout (RPC already `statement_timeout=60s`). Real cause: the edge fn calls `upsert_pack_rips_from_api` (SECDEF, service_role) but the PostgREST session connects via `authenticator`, whose session-preloaded **`lock_timeout=8s` survives `SET ROLE`** and applies inside the RPC (which only overrode statement_timeout). Overlapping backfill invocations walk the SAME `after_cursor` and upsert the SAME `pack_nft_id` rows → the second contends on `pack_rips` locks and dies at 8s (each real page-upsert is sub-second). **Fix 1 (DB, LIVE):** migration adds `lock_timeout=25s` to the RPC so a brief overlap waits it out instead of failing (grants unchanged: postgres+service_role, no anon). **Fix 2 (edge, needs deploy):** per-collection `claim/release_pipeline_lock` guard in `backfill-pack-opens-api` so overlapping runs cleanly no-op (fail-open, 300s stale). **Verified:** since the migration, 5 consecutive allday ticks `ok=true`, `rips_total` 1,141,298→1,221,269 (~20k/tick), **0 lock-timeout failures** — incl. a 17:20:20Z tick where topshot+allday fired the same second and both passed. **Revert:** `ALTER FUNCTION public.upsert_pack_rips_from_api(jsonb) RESET lock_timeout;` + `git revert c1ba51e`.
- **`topshot-moments-hydrator` — "gql errors: Error with GetMintedMoment" ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (needs CF worker deploy).** Client bug, NOT TopShot's API down (50 moments/run resolve fine). `fetchChunk` discarded the **entire 50-id aliased chunk** whenever `json.errors` was non-empty — but GraphQL returns **partial data**: one burned/retired moment nulls only its own alias while the other 49 succeed. One poison id wasted 49 good lookups and let the permanent tail of unresolvable ids at the queue head (`v_moments_needing_hydration`) starve throughput → the observed alternating ok=false / `fetched_from_graphql:0` runs. **Fix:** parse `json.data` even when `errors` present; unresolved aliases fall through as `graphql_failures` (now counted, previously vanished). Separate hard chunk failures (HTTP/network/parse — no data) from normal per-id upstream errors; only hard failures (or a 0-row write with resolvable rows) flip `ok=false`. Adds `hard_chunk_failures` telemetry. Worker typecheck passes. **Revert:** `git revert c1ba51e`.
- **DEPLOY NEEDED (noted, not done — no push/deploy per constraint):** (1) Supabase edge fn `backfill-pack-opens-api` (concurrency guard — belt-and-suspenders; the DB lock_timeout fix already stopped the failures). (2) CF worker `topshot-moments-hydrator` (`wrangler deploy` — this is what activates the #3 fix; until deployed the hydrator keeps discarding poisoned chunks). Commit `c1ba51e` is on local `main`, unpushed.
- **Left untouched:** the 2 pre-existing unstaged edits (`edition/[slug]/page.tsx`, `moment/[id]/page.tsx`) from concurrent work. No FMV-calc code touched.

### 2026-07-11 (Claude Code, interactive) — `fmv-recalc` Step-1a `edition_page_fetch` statement-timeout FIXED (dedicated 120s-timeout SECDEF fn + covering index)

`fmv-recalc` was logging intermittent `edition_page_fetch: canceling statement due to statement timeout` (3 consecutive fails at report time; scattered pairs across the day, clustering at higher OFFSET 2500/5000/7500). **Root cause:** Step-1a's edition-page query (`SELECT edition_id FROM sales WHERE sold_at >= now()-30d AND price_usd>0 AND collection_id<>pinnacle AND edition_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY edition_id ORDER BY MAX(sold_at) DESC LIMIT/OFFSET`) ran through the generic `query_sql` RPC, which inherits the **service_role 30s statement_timeout**. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` = **31.2s cold vs 0.18s warm** — the 30-day window now spans ~110K sales rows / ~11,953 distinct editions, and with no `sold_at`-leading index the planner does a full scan of `sales_2026_collection_id_sold_at_idx` (collection_id leading, unusable for a sold_at-only range) + ~110K heap fetches (~18.5K cold blocks). Not a code regression — organic sales-volume growth pushed the cold scan just past 30s; warm runs (most) passed, cold/contended runs failed. Confirmed via `pipeline_runs` (ok=true runs interleaved with the timeouts).

- **SHIPPED (DB) — `fmv_recalc_edition_page(timestamptz, uuid, int, int)`** (`audit_20260711_fmv_recalc_edition_page_fn_120s_timeout` + `_revoke_anon`). Dedicated SECURITY DEFINER fn, `SET statement_timeout=120s` + `search_path=public` in proconfig (mirrors `query_sql`'s RLS-bypass so behavior is identical), **service_role-only** (REVOKE anon+authenticated — Supabase default-privs re-grant them on new public fns; `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` []). Output verified byte-identical to the inline query (2500/2500 rows, full INTERSECT overlap). Gives the page fetch deterministic headroom regardless of planner/cache state (120s ≫ 31s cold worst case). Revert: `DROP FUNCTION public.fmv_recalc_edition_page(timestamptz, uuid, integer, integer);`
- **SHIPPED (DB) — covering index `idx_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window`** (`audit_20260711_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window_covering_index`) `ON sales_2026 (sold_at DESC) INCLUDE (edition_id, collection_id) WHERE price_usd>0 AND edition_id IS NOT NULL`. Once autovacuum lifts `sales_2026` visibility (currently 74% all-visible; the query targets the newest, least-visible pages), the planner switches to a fast index-only scan and the cold path drops from ~31s to ~sub-second — the 120s ceiling becomes a safety floor, never the steady state. Non-concurrent build (MCP wraps DDL in a txn so `CONCURRENTLY` is unavailable; 492MB partition built in <1s under a brief ShareLock, harmless to cursor-based sales ingest). Revert: `DROP INDEX public.idx_sales_2026_fmv_recalc_window;`
- **SHIPPED (code `e2f3922`, deploy `dpl_9kd98rsU2UiKTZZC3LtqVdyTkovf`)** — route Step-1a now calls `fmv_recalc_edition_page` instead of the inline `query_sql`. Additive, single call-site swap; response shape unchanged (`{edition_id}[]`). Revert: `git revert e2f3922`.
- Relation to the standing **FMV-RECALC-EDITION-FETCH-TIMEOUT-CREEP** ledger watch (DB-growth contention) — this is that creep crossing the hard 30s wall; now fixed deterministically.

### 2026-07-04 (daytime, Claude Code — marketplace-status stale-banner fix) — client hook force-cache pinned pre-07-03 "unknown" status

- **SHIPPED (code) — `useMarketplaceStatus` fetch `force-cache` → `no-cache`.** While Chrome-verifying the Golazos hero I noticed the edition page STILL showed the "No confirmed Flow marketplace" banner despite the 07-03 `collection_config` flip to healthy. Traced it: the DB + API are correct (`v_collection_marketplace_status` golazos = healthy/buy_ctas_enabled=true; live `GET /api/marketplace-status?collection=laliga-golazos` with `no-store` returns **healthy**), but the client hook `components/marketplace-status/useMarketplaceStatus.ts` fetched with `cache:"force-cache"` — which returns the browser's HTTP-cache copy **fresh OR stale**, ignoring the route's `s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60`. A live `force-cache` fetch returned the stale pre-fix **unknown/buy_ctas=false**. So any visitor who loaded Golazos before 07-03 kept seeing the old banner + suppressed buy CTAs indefinitely (until browser eviction), never reaching the intended 5-min refresh; symmetrically it would keep buy CTAs live after a collection went UNhealthy. The stated reason for `force-cache` (one call per slug per session) is already met by the module-level `memoryCache`/`inflight` dedup, so `force-cache` only added staleness. Switched to `cache:"no-cache"` (revalidate; the CDN `s-maxage=300` still absorbs load). Affects the banner + every client marketplace-status consumer (sniper/market/collection/overview rows). tsc clean (changed file). No FMV/pricing. **Revert:** `git revert` (cache mode back to `force-cache`).

### 2026-07-03 (daytime, Claude Code) — shipped 2 HIGH items to main: topshot-sales-history-backfill 429-resilience (Item 1) + Bug 13 restored the moment-page LISTED field off cached_listings_v2. tsc clean (changed files); no DB change

Direct-to-main. Both are code-only. Follows the earlier 07-03 Cowork queue cleanup (32 phantom→empty / 13 frozen→pending) above.

- **Item 1 (topshot-sales-history-backfill 429 storm).** The pipeline was hard rate-limited on ~every TS GQL call — ticks completed in ~0s draining nothing while ~5.6K editions sat pending. Fix spans two files:
  - `lib/chains/flow/topshot.ts` — `topshotGraphql` gained an **opt-in** 3rd arg `TopshotGraphqlOptions { retryOn429, maxRetries, maxBackoffMs }`. When `retryOn429` is set, a 429 is retried honoring the server `Retry-After` header (delta-seconds OR HTTP-date), falling back to exponential backoff (2s·2^n) + jitter, each sleep capped by `maxBackoffMs`. **Default OFF → every existing caller (sniper-feed, badge-sync, …) is byte-identical; zero blast radius.**
  - `app/api/cron/topshot-sales-history-backfill/route.ts` — opts in via `GQL_OPTS { retryOn429, maxRetries:2, maxBackoffMs:8000 }` on both GQL call sites; adds a `GQL_THROTTLE_MS=250` sleep before every set-map/tx page fetch; adds an `INTER_EDITION_DELAY_MS=350` sleep between editions; drops `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` 120→15 (small batch — hundreds/tick just re-trips the limiter); and adds attempt-counter integrity — an edition that exhausts `MAX_EDITION_ATTEMPTS` on a retryable (gql/setmap) error is now counted (`editions_maxed_out`, surfaced in the `pipeline_runs.extra` + a `console.log`) instead of silently freezing in `error` status. Bounded: worst-case retry adds ~16s to one call, well inside `maxDuration=300` with the between-edition budget break. **Verify:** watch `pipeline_runs WHERE pipeline='topshot-sales-history-backfill'` — runs should show `sales_inserted>0` / declining `pending_remaining` once the queue clears. **Revert:** `git revert` the two-file commit (DB untouched; the opt-in param is inert for all other callers).
  - Note: the route calls `public-api.nbatopshot.com` directly (via `topshotGraphql`), not the proxy — 429 (not 403) confirms the requests reach the API; the fix is rate-pacing, not a routing change.
  - **Follow-up (same day, `921f5fc`): `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` 15→40.** A post-deploy `workflow_dispatch` tick verified the fix live — 15 editions ran with only **2 `gql_errors`** (~13% vs the ~83% pre-fix; 13/15 drained, 0 maxed_out, budget NOT hit). Since the batch cap (not the limiter) was bounding throughput on the finite ~5.6K queue, raised to 40 so the 240s `ELAPSED_BUDGET_MS` is the limiter again (throttle + inter-edition delay govern API pressure per call regardless of batch), draining ~2x faster at the same low error rate. Deliberately exceeds the prompt's "5-10/run" (that was a proxy for "don't burst," now enforced by the throttle). **Revert:** set `EDITIONS_PER_TICK` back to 15 (or `git revert 921f5fc`).
- **Item 2 (Bug 13 — restore moment-page LISTED field).** The earlier 07-03 entry HID the field because its only source (`ts_listings`) is dead. This restores it from `cached_listings_v2` — the live on-chain listing feed (currently 21,999 active AllDay listings / 20,900 flow_ids; Golazos 0 right now; no TS rows yet). `app/moment/[id]/page.tsx`: new `fetchActiveListingAsk(nftId)` does `DISTINCT ON`-equivalent (`.eq(flow_id) .is(completed_at,null) .order(price_usd asc) .limit(1)`) → cheapest active ask; wired into the serial-block `Promise.all` (kind='moment' only, keyed on `ss.nft_id`); renders a single `Listed` StatCell (`fmtUsd`, dash when unlisted). ### 2026-07-02 (daytime, Claude Code) — P8 WRITER GUARD SHIPPED: found + fixed the 5th moments-writer (the hydrator's ambiguous (set,play)→edition map); leak stopped, drain now durable

The updated handoff flagged that P8's corrupt-moments set is NOT finite — ~325/24h are actively created by an unidentified 5th moments-writer, so firing the `?p8=1` drain once just re-accumulates. Found the writer, root-caused it, and guarded the write chokepoint. 1 commit (`1cd46de`) + 1 migration (applied via MCP `audit_20260702_replace_topshot_moments_batch_parallel_guard`, repo-synced `supabase/migrations/20260702150000_*`); `check_public_security_invariants()` **[]**; verified live end-to-end.

- **The 5th writer = `topshot-moments-hydrator`** (worker, every 10 min, ~265 moments/run). Its `resolveEditions()` (workers/topshot-moments-hydrator/index.ts L289-298) selects editions by `(set_id_onchain, play_id_onchain)` and builds a `${set}:${play}`→edition uuid map — but the **2026-06-20 subedition catalog cloned those on-chain ids onto every `::` parallel**, so that pair is non-unique (base + all parallels share it) and the map is **overwritten by whichever row PostgREST returns last**. A small-circ `::` parallel can win → a Standard moment lands on it (serial > parallel circ = impossible). NOT the `/api/ingest` `buildEditionKey` (that's submap-gated + 97% of corrupt nfts aren't in the submap), NOT a circulation backfill.
- **Evidence (re-measured live):** 464 corrupt; **328 moment-side inserts/24h, edition-side untouched (0)**, `created_at==updated_at` (fresh inserts of new nfts); the SALES for these nfts sit on **base** (`sale_on_same_parallel=0` all sources) = moment-only mis-key; **452/464 not in `topshot_moment_subeditions`**; **114/114 corrupt `::`editions share (set,play) with a base sibling**; hydrator runs time-correlate to the newest corrupt insert (21:02Z).
- **Fix (root-cause, at the write chokepoint) — `replace_topshot_moments_batch(jsonb)`.** This SECDEF RPC is where every moments writer actually lands rows, so the guard lives here (mirrors the sales-indexer Step-4e + offer_fill base-redirect). A `redirected` CTE, applied **before** the `(edition_id,serial_number)` dedupe (so post-redirect collisions collapse instead of tripping `ON CONFLICT ... cannot affect row a second time`), rewrites any incoming moment on a `::`parallel with `serial > that parallel's circulation` to the **base** `setID:playID` edition; genuine subedition moments (serial ≤ circ) pass through untouched. Catches the hydrator AND any future caller.
- **Deliberately did NOT force base in the hydrator worker.** The hydrator can't place genuine parallels (no submap); forcing all (set,play) resolutions to base would re-collide genuine parallel serials with base serials — the exact conflation the `::`-split solved. The DB guard only touches the unambiguously-impossible case (serial > parallel circ), leaving genuine-parallel placement to the existing submap-driven `remap_topshot_base_keyed_parallel_sales()`.
- **Verified live (MCP):** (1) end-to-end RPC probe — `replace_topshot_moments_batch` with a Standard serial 11 keyed onto `222:7443::20` (circ 10) → **landed on base `222:7443`** (test row cleaned up, no real moment touched); (2) negative replay — **0/500** existing genuine parallels would be redirected; (3) **two** post-guard hydrator cycles (**21:12Z + 21:22Z**, ~268 moments each) → **0 new corrupt** (newest corrupt still 21:02Z, the last pre-guard run; vs the pre-guard ~2–3/run); (4) `check_public_security_invariants()` **[]**.
- **Consequence: `?p8=1` (24fec11) is now a durable one-shot.** New impossible mis-keys are blocked, so the existing 464 are a finite set the drain cleans on firing (operator/deployed, proxy creds). The 175 colliders still need on-chain truth (the drain's `remap_topshot_from_onchain_map()` free-slot leg handles them); the 281 non-colliders could alternatively be bulk-redirected to base via the same guard logic if the operator prefers not to fire the drain. **Revert:** restore the prior function body from `supabase/migrations/20260517131500_replace_topshot_moments_batch_on_conflict_do_update.sql` (+ `git revert 1cd46de`).

Item 4's HIGH sales indexers already got a backstop (`cfe034e`); this is the families it correctly left out because they can't be naively double-fired. **Key reframe (correct):** the hazard is NOT dup rows (both families are already row-idempotent — `upsert_wmc_batch ON CONFLICT`, snapshot UPSERT on `(wallet,collection,snapshot_at)`), it's **2× on-chain Cadence per wallet + connection-pool/IO saturation (the 2026-06-10 DBSAT class)**. So: make a concurrent invocation a NO-OP FIRST, then the backstop needs NO atomic cutover. 1 commit (`611b2fb`), 1 migration, 1 edge-fn redeploy, 2 GHA workflows; tsc clean; security 0/0/0/0; deploy READY.

- **DB — `audit_20260627_pipeline_run_locks_concurrency_guard` (service_role only).** New `pipeline_run_locks(lock_key pk, status, claimed_at, released_at, attempts)` (RLS on, anon/auth REVOKEd) + `claim_pipeline_lock(p_key, p_stale_seconds default 660)` / `release_pipeline_lock(p_key)`. **Claim-row pattern (mirrors `allow_list_claim_prewarm`), deliberately NOT an advisory xact lock** — a PostgREST-driven walk spans many separate transactions, so `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` would auto-release after the first call and protect nothing; a durable claim row survives the multi-second walk and across separate lambdas. Atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE (status='done' OR claimed_at < now()-stale)` → a fresh in_progress returns false (no-op); a `done`/stale row is reclaimable. Stale=660s is safely **above** the 600s maxDuration ceiling on the heaviest child, so a legitimately-running long walk is never falsely stale, while a hard-killed lambda's lock self-clears in ≤11 min. **Verified live:** claim→true, 2nd claim→false (blocked), release→done, reclaim→true; stale=0 always reclaims; security invariants 0, secdef-anon 0, tables_without_rls 0.
- **Guard helper — [lib/wallet-backfill-lock.ts]** (`claimPipelineLock`/`releasePipelineLock`, key `wallet-backfill:<slug>:<wallet>`). **FAIL-OPEN**: any lock RPC error/throw → claim returns true (proceed), so the guard can NEVER become a new SPOF that halts ingest. Per-(collection,wallet) key so the 5 children for one wallet never block each other (the multicollection orchestrator fans them out concurrently).
- **Family #2 wiring (the expensive one — overlap = 2× Cadence/wallet).** Guard at the top of `runBackfill` (TS, [app/api/wallet-backfill/route.ts]) + the 3 shared runners in [lib/chains/flow/wallet-backfill-helpers.ts] — `runIdOnlyBackfill` (golazos+ufc), `runAllDayDetailsBackfill`, `runPinnacleDetailsBackfill`. A concurrent walk no-ops: fire-and-forget runners log `terminated_reason=skipped_in_progress` + return rowsFound 0; the sync runners (allday/pinnacle) additionally return `complete:true` so the orchestrator stops polling that collection for that wallet. Released in `finally`. `runPaginatedDetailsBackfill` is internal-only (called inside the guarded allday/pinnacle runners) so it's intentionally NOT separately guarded.
- **Family #1 wiring (snapshot — read-only, belt-and-suspenders).** Guard added to the edge fn `runWork` (claim at the `Deno.serve` call site, try/finally release, skip→logs `skipped_in_progress`). **Edge fn redeployed v10→v11** (`verify_jwt=false` preserved).
- **Backstops (redundant, harmless thanks to the guard — NO cutover):** [.github/workflows/wallet-backfill-backstop.yml] fires the 4 `seed-wallet-refresh?cohort=K&of=4` cohorts at `38 2,8,14,20` UTC (GHA-empty minute, ~2h after each primary 6h window, staggered 60s). ### 2026-07-16 (Cowork interactive) — ALLDAY-UNMAPPED-SALES-BACKLOG DRAINED via browser relay (6,539 sales recovered)
- The AllDay consumer GQL (`nflallday.com/consumer/graphql` `searchMomentNFTsV2(byFlowIDs)` — the only OWNER-INDEPENDENT moment->edition index) WAF-blocks EVERY non-browser lane: Vercel, Supabase edge, the topshot-proxy CF worker `/allday-consumer` route (probed: WAF block page), AND residential curl on Trevor's machine (the home-fill script got the block page). ONLY a real browser on the nflallday.com origin (same-origin fetch) passes. That's why the live `allday-unmapped-resolver` (which routes through the now-blocked worker) couldn't drain it and the backlog grew to ~8,846.
- DRAINED via a Chrome-session relay: resolve batches of 1,000 target ids on an nflallday.com tab -> carry the resolved rows in `window.name` across a cross-origin navigation (URL-hash echoes flooded tokens; window.name is clean) -> a rippackscity.com tab POSTs them to a temp confirm-guarded edge bridge (`allday-unmapped-bridge`, now 410-stubbed) which does mapping upsert (`resolve_unmapped_sales_for_collection` p_promote_limit=0) + `promote_unmapped_sales`; ids the owner-independent GQL never returns are marked `unmapped_sales_resolution_failures.retry_count=5` so `get_unmapped_resolver_targets` skips them (its exclusion rule) and the head keeps advancing. **Result: 6,539 sales promoted into public.sales this session; 2,199 genuinely-dead ids retired; `get_unmapped_resolver_targets` now returns 0.** AllDay sales-based FMV/analytics no longer undercount recoverable recent secondary volume.
- Also `df5a733`: deleted the WAF-dead `scripts/allday-unmapped-fill.mjs` (residential curl blocked); kept the transport-agnostic `/api/admin/allday-unmapped-fill` route (annotated browser-driven-only) for any future browser filler. Softened the combative `/insights` SEO taglines (`90115fb`, Trevor: "Things Top Shot won't tell you" too aggressive). Rescued the stranded 2026-07-15 weekly-sweep ledger entry (`e5e7953`).
- STANDING NOTE (verified 2026-07-16): the residual ~2,300 dead ids are moments not in AllDay's owner-independent index (burned/invalid/very old) — genuinely unrecoverable; NOT a pipeline bug, do not re-chase. **Ongoing inflow is already correctly monitored + bounded — no durable automation needed.** The on-chain `allday-resolve-unmapped` (Vercel, WAF-proof) handles most fresh inflow; the trust-health metric `unmapped_resolution_backlog_max` counts only RECENT (30d) priced-sale resolution stalls (aged residual excluded by design) and pages at breach 100 (currently **25**, ok). So the FMV-relevant recent undercount stays small and visible. - **OFFER-SANITY-RAISE · 2026-06-09 (data-quality sweep, recommend) · [LOW-MED · CC — edition_offers writer, off-limits to the passes] schedule the durable GREATEST-based `edition_offers.highest_offer` raise.** `v_offer_sanity_flags` = 174 (was 132 on 06-07); composition stable + structural: 138 (79%) are `chain_exceeds_gql`+sub_serial (GQL collapses subedition/serial offers; max gap $658), 21 `gql_blank_chain_has` (the 12 non-subedition ones carry the headline gaps — SGA Kingmaker $5,222, LeBron Supernova $5,000, Wilt $1,501). Growth tracks on-chain offer accrual, not a fault. Durable fix (per `rpc-offers-data-model` memory): raise `edition_offers.highest_offer` via `GREATEST(existing, chain_open_max)` — never clobber down — keyed off the on-chain `offers` open-max, in a CC-owned job; recurring raise (slowly grows), not a one-time backfill. Sweep did NOT write edition_offers (task-forbidden). **CLASSIFICATION LOCKED 2026-06-09 (Trevor):** `offers.offer_type` is 3 nested grains, each displays at its OWN grain — **edition** (universal across the edition), **subedition** (that subedition only), **serial** (that one serial only). The edition "Best offer" cell may be raised ONLY by `offer_type='edition'` (a serial/subedition bid is not the edition floor). Open volumes: edition 5,284 / subedition 1,541 / serial 535. Validated raise scope = `GREATEST(existing, max(offers WHERE offer_type='edition' AND status='open'))`: the REAL edition-cell gap is just **14 editions** (`gql_blank_chain_has`, ~$17.2k total, max $5,222 SGA Kingmaker / $5,000 LeBron Supernova / $1,501 Wilt); the other 13 edition-grain flags are penny noise ($14 total) and the 147 sub/serial flags are correctly out-of-scope. Small + safe. Subedition offers → a subedition-grain surface; serial offers → that serial's moment view. Detail: `docs/data-quality-sweep-2026-06-09.md`.

  SHIPPED (CC, commit `bd8f663`, deploy `dpl_5J9aTFbz4vG85LusJP4J7a5Pe7TS` READY): the badge-sync sweep was capped at MAX_PAGES(20)×100 = 2,000 editions/badge; raised to 80 (+`maxDuration=300`, PAGE_DELAY 400→250). BUT a full sweep grew the table only +23 (3,012→3,035 TS rows): the `POST /api/badge-sync` run logged `upserted:2006, upsertErrors:28` — ~1,400 collected rows dropped. ROOT CAUSE: the upsert uses `onConflict:"id"` but the table also has `badge_editions_ext_coll_unique UNIQUE(external_id,collection_id)`; parallels of the same play share an `external_id` but differ in `id`, so a parallel with a new id takes INSERT → violates the unique constraint → fails the WHOLE 50-row supabase-js batch. The lifted cap surfaces MORE parallels → more poisoned batches. Existing rows are a mix (2,819 parallel_id=0 + ~216 non-zero) so the table's row-grain is itself ambiguous (PK embeds parallel; unique key collapses to one-per-play). FIX (needs a row-grain decision + Trevor review — not rushed): decide one-row-per-play vs per-parallel, align `onConflict` + the unique constraint, and dedup the sweep by `external_id` in code to avoid "ON CONFLICT … cannot affect row a second time". NOT auto-shippable (touches the badge write path + a constraint). Memory: badge-editions-key-format-and-upsert-poison.

### audit_20260705_widen_pack_ev_value_ratio_full
- **What:** Widened `pack_ev_history.value_ratio` NUMERIC(6,3) → NUMERIC(12,4). Dropped and recreated all 15 dependent views/MVs atomically in a single transaction.

Root cause: packs with very low price but high constituent FMV produce `gross_ev / pack_price > 999.999`, exceeding the old column max. `topshot_pack_reality_top_ev` was stuck at 7 rows (only the packs under 999.999 succeeded).
- **Verified:** Column confirmed NUMERIC(12,4) via `information_schema.columns`. All 3 MV indexes recreated. All 9 security_invoker=on views confirmed. Pack EV board will repopulate automatically on next cron-job.org pipeline tick.
- **Revert:** Rerun the same drop/alter/recreate cycle with NUMERIC(6,3) — this restores the overflow bug, so revert is only meaningful if a data corruption issue surfaces.

### compute-topshot-pack-ev v22 (edge fn, deployed via MCP; repo copy committed this push)
- **ROOT CAUSE of the 306 "$0 EV on live packs" (incl. 2026 Finals/WNBA/Playoffs flagships): pool-insert PK collision.** Probe (temp edge fn `tmp-pack-pool-probe`, now 410-stubbed) proved `packEditionsV3` returns one node PER SLOT — the same edition appears in >=2 nodes on multi-slot packs (8520: 10 dupes of 29 editions; 8548: 6; 8564: 2). `pack_drop_pool`'s PK is `(collection_id, dist_id, edition_id, slot_name)` with `slot_name='default'` hard-coded -> the entire insert chunk failed 23505 AFTER the pool delete had run -> pool left EMPTY every tick -> `no_varied_remaining_pool` -> $0 sentinel, deterministically, forever (8514 never had a real EV since 05-22; the API had full real data the whole time — probe showed 8548 with 1,407 unopened + real per-edition remaining). **v22 merges duplicate editions (sum count + remaining) before insert.**

- **Ask fallback:** `fetchSecondaryAskMap` now fills missing entries from `pack_ask_state` (canonical) — writer-side dual price no longer misses live asks (secondary_asks_count 1,950/tick, was Studio-only).
- **verify_jwt GOTCHA (memory updated):** MCP `deploy_edge_function` RESET `verify_jwt` false->true on redeploy, which would have 401'd the cron trigger (non-JWT Bearer). Caught immediately; toggled back OFF via the dashboard (Chrome). **Any future MCP redeploy of a cron-triggered fn must re-check verify_jwt.**

## 2026-07-16 (Cowork, interactive, continuation 4) — THE core Pack-EV inaccuracy found + guarded: chase-biased public-API pools

Accuracy validation pass on the now-repriced board surfaced the real reason "the numbers still don't seem accurate" on CURRENT packs. The 2026 Finals Standard (8548) showed $37 gross vs $18 ask (2x). Root cause: **packEditionsV3 returns a CHASE-BIASED edition list** — 8548's own remaining_by_tier says 4,564 commons / 958 rares / 4 legendaries still sealed, but the pool the API gave us had only 1 common edition + 4 legendaries. The per-slot RPC normalizes over that survivor set, so a handful of $772/$248 legendaries (2 copies left each) drag the mean to $37 while the TYPICAL pull is a $6 common. Same on 8520 WNBA ($45, driven by one genuinely-$48 Olivia Miles rookie common that was 79% of a pool holding only 149 of 8,695 real remaining moments).

**Rigorous completeness guard (audit_20260716_pack_ev_pool_completeness_guard, supersedes the same-day tier-fraction guard):** a COMPLETE per-slot remaining pool must have `sum(drop_weight) = sum(remaining)/total_unopened >= moments_per_pack >= 1`. Observed: complete pools (Atlas harvests, chance-hit packs) sum to 0.89-1.0; chase-biased packEditionsV3 pools sum to <0.08 (8548 0.038, 8520 0.075, 8601 0.009) — a clean 10x+ gap needing no tier/slot data. `compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted` now returns ok:false 'pool_incomplete' when TS sum(drop_weight)<0.5 → no writer emits chase-inflated EV; single-edition packs (sum_dw>=1) and Atlas pools pass. (The earlier tier-fraction guard caught 8548 but missed 8520, whose few captured commons happened to include the $48 rookie — the fraction looked fine while absolute coverage was 1.7%.)

**Routed to Atlas + flipped live:** `v_topshot_atlas_pool_targets` now also includes chase-incomplete gql pools (sum_dw<0.5) + adds 'atlas_refresh' for restaleing atlas pools — 174 targets (146 incomplete_pool). Wrote qualifying sentinels for the 97 currently-inflated incomplete dists (pack_price=ask so they supersede in pack_ev_latest's price>0 filter) → they now show honest "no EV" immediately. Verified live on pack_table_rows: 8548/8520/8564/8601 → NULL EV (honest); Grail Seeker $0.75, Birthday Party $3.23, Courtside $3.87 (Atlas-complete) → real EV. security 0/0/0/0.

**NET honest state:** Pack EV shows a real number ONLY where the pool is complete (Atlas-harvested or genuinely complete); chase-incomplete packs show "no EV" instead of a fabricated one. Re-running the Atlas harvest (`scripts/atlas-pool-harvest.ps1`, now 174 targets) gives the current flagship packs (Finals/WNBA/Playoffs) real complete-pool EVs — the differentiator. **Reverts:** restore prior compute_pack_ev_per_edition_weighted + v_topshot_atlas_pool_targets defs from migration history; the 97 sentinel rows age out as real EV rows land. **Deferred (Trevor decision):** the median/typical-pull display signal — even a complete-pool mean EV overstates the typical outcome for lottery-shaped packs; a "typical pull $X / jackpot $Y" UI split would be more honest than a single mean, but that's a frontend change (handoff), not shipped.

Added `pack_ev_history.typical_ev numeric(10,2)`. Both share the completeness + varied-pool guards.
- **audit_20260716_expose_typical_ev_in_read_stack:** recreated `mv_pack_ev_latest` (matview) + `pack_table_rows` + `pack_ev_latest` to carry `typical_ev` (appended at end; sentinel-nulled like gross_ev).
